summary.title: Language-agnosticism #36: member_access_patterns grammar fact
summary.what: Added Grammar.member_access_patterns() (base default empty) with per-grammar overrides from a verified (node_type, receiver_field) table across all 11 grammars; rewrote profile._receiver_call_count to iterate the callable's own patterns instead of hardcoded Python attribute/subscript; threaded each callable's grammar through clusters._bodies_index -> profile_cluster. Added test_receiver_density.py. Suite 199->204.
summary.why: The receiver-call-density signal — which drives the first-param-cluster missing_class/dispatch_family classification — read 0 on every non-Python language because it matched only Python node types. Same silent-deadening class as the extract_parameters root bug: 'not flagged' was masquerading as 'clean' on Go/Rust/Java/etc.

decisions.point: Worklist item #35 (receiver_parameter_names grammar fact) — build it or not?
decisions.chose: Dropped it as a verified no-op; not built.
decisions.rationale: Probed all 11 grammars: {self, cls} is correct for Python and a no-op everywhere else — no other language puts its receiver in the parameter list (Go separate receiver field, Rust &self keyword node, Java/C++/C#/Ruby implicit). A uniform constant is not a language branch, so making it a grammar fact is churn without a correctness change. This overrode the pre-compaction plan, which had mischaracterized #35 as a bug.
rejected: Building receiver_parameter_names() per the plan's stated sequence

decisions.chose: A (node_type, receiver_field) tuple list iterated by a language-neutral consumer
decisions.rationale: Keeps _receiver_call_count free of any language branching, matching the tabular-dispatch contract; node types are language-specific so a single hardcoded set silently zeroes every other language.

decisions.point: How profile_cluster reaches each member's language
decisions.chose: Thread the grammar object through _bodies_index, not a precomputed pattern set
decisions.rationale: A cluster can span languages; carrying the grammar lets each member resolve its own member-access patterns correctly.

decisions.point: C# member-access patterns when the tree-sitter-c-sharp wheel does not parse
decisions.chose: Declare best-effort patterns from the grammar's node-type names, flagged unverified in-code
decisions.rationale: Honest non-deferral rather than silent omission; revisit when C# parses. Cannot be live-verified in this environment.

rejected.reason: Verified unnecessary — {self, cls} is correct for Python and a no-op for every other language.
